title: Rust: Singleton Pattern
description: Implement the singleton pattern using OnceCell and global statics in Rust.

steps.title: Basic Singleton with OnceCell
steps.description: Use `std::sync::OnceLock` (Rust 1.70+) to create a thread-safe singleton that stores a `String`. Set it once and read it multiple times.

verification.failureMessage: Set and print the singleton value.

steps.title: Lazy Initialization
steps.description: Use `std::sync::LazyLock` (or `once_cell::sync::Lazy`) for lazy initialization. Create a singleton that initializes on first access. Print the value.
hints: The closure runs only once on first access.
Access twice: first triggers init, second just reads.

verification.failureMessage: Access the lazy singleton and print its value.

steps.title: Mutex Singleton for Mutable State
steps.description: Create a mutable singleton using `OnceLock<Mutex<HashMap<String, String>>>`. Provide `set(key, val)` and `get(key)` functions. Test by storing and retrieving values.

verification.failureMessage: Store and retrieve a value from the singleton HashMap.

steps.title: Thread-Safe Singleton Access
steps.description: Test your mutable singleton with multiple threads. Spawn 5 threads, each setting a different key-value pair. After joining, print all values from the singleton.
hints: Clone the DB reference (but Mutex handles the inner data).
After threads finish, print all entries.

verification.failureMessage: 5 threads write to the singleton, verify all values present.

steps.title: Singleton with Default Config
steps.description: Create a `Config` struct with default values and a singleton that loads once. Include fields like `db_url`, `port`, `debug_mode`. Print the config values.
hints: `struct Config { db_url: String, port: u16, debug: bool }`

verification.failureMessage: Initialize and print the Config singleton.
